Priya (CS): FYI — Aurora Therapeutics asked for a one-pager SLA summary to attach to procurement. They want uptime, latency targets, how credits are calculated, and a short onboarding timeline. Renewal conversation in ~6 weeks. Can @Liam (SRE) and @Jordan (Solutions) confirm numbers so we can draft?
Liam (SRE): quick answer: hosted API SLO = 99.9% monthly availability; p95 latency target 350ms for standard routes. For Dedicated we typically commit 99.95% but note warm-up for model variants can bump p95 to ~700ms for the first hour after deploy.
Jordan (Solutions): noted. Also we need to call out pinned model/version and KV cache warm-up notes in the doc. Suggested wording: "Latency SLOs measured on steady-state production traffic; initial rollout/scale windows may show transient increases."
Priya (CS): thanks. For credits — do we have a standard proration formula we can share? Customers want a straight example line too.
Liam (SRE): use the standard monthly-proration calc we use for other contracts. Example snippet we can paste: ```credit = round(min(0.3, max(0, (SLO_target - observed_availability) / SLO_target)) * committed_monthly_fee, 2)``` so max credit cap = 30% of monthly committed spend.
Jordan (Solutions): add an example row: "Committed: $10,000/mo — Observed availability 99.6% vs target 99.9% => shortfall 0.3% => credit = min(30%, 0.003/0.999 * 100%) * $10,000 ≈ $30". Keep math clear, customers like the simple table.
Amir (AE): good. From renewal risk POV Aurora is heavy on inference volume ramp — they care about predictable latency under burst. Can we add recommended guardrails (burst protection, reserved concurrency, pre-warming) they can buy as Dedicated add-on?
Jordan (Solutions): yes: list options: Dedicated reserved pool, autoscale ceiling, pre-warm runbook, optional warm-up traffic window. Also call out expected lead time for Dedicated capacity (2-3 weeks).
Priya (CS): action items: (1) Liam — confirm the exact monthly availability metric name we should reference (e.g., "monthly uptime percentage (MUP)") and paste the monitoring query we can include as evidence link; (2) Jordan — draft the one-pager language + example table; (3) Amir — coordinate pricing add-ons and comms for renewal team. I’ll assemble and send to Aurora by EOD Friday.
Liam (SRE): confirmed metric name = "monthly uptime percentage (MUP)". Monitoring query (Prometheus-ish) to link: `sum_over_time(up{job=\"inference\"}[30d]) / (30*24*3600)` — will create evidence dashboard and share link.
Jordan (Solutions): drafting now. Will include the short onboarding timeline: Week 0: kickoff + API keys; Week 1: integration + test traffic; Week 2: performance tuning + canary; Week 3: scale to prod.
Amir (AE): I’ll prep the Dedicated add-on pricing sheet and flag renewal owner. Also recommend a pre-emptive customer call once we share the doc.
Priya (CS): perfect. Can everyone add their final snippets to the shared doc here: <https://redwood.docs/aurora-sla-summary-draft> by Thursday 12:00 PT? I’ll consolidate and send. :thumbsup:
OnboardBot: Reminder scheduled — notify thread members 2024-04-11T12:00:00Z.
Liam (SRE): added dashboard link and short example logs. small note: for multi-region routing the effective SLO may vary; state that multi-region customers get regional SLOs and aggregated SLA is per-region.
Priya (CS): good catch. Adding that note. Thanks all — will ping if auditors ask for raw evidence. :raised_hands:
